history: Oulton Park, nestled in the Cheshire countryside, boasts a rich history dating back to 1953. Originally a military training ground during World War II, it was transformed into a racing circuit by the Mid-Cheshire Car Club. The International layout, one of the most popular configurations, has hosted countless prestigious events, including rounds of the British Touring Car Championship (BTCC), British GT Championship, and the British Superbike Championship (BSB). Its challenging nature and picturesque setting have made it a favourite among drivers and spectators alike. The circuit's evolution reflects the changing demands of motorsport, with safety improvements and track modifications made over the years to accommodate increasingly powerful and sophisticated racing machinery.
atmosphere: Standing on the banks at Oulton Park's International circuit during a BTCC race weekend is an assault on the senses. The air crackles with anticipation as the tin-tops scream past, their engines echoing through the trees. The smell of burning rubber and high-octane fuel hangs heavy, mingling with the aroma of burgers from the food stalls. The roar of the crowd rises and falls with every overtake and incident, creating an electric atmosphere that is both exhilarating and captivating. The close proximity of the track to the spectator areas provides an unrivaled view of the action, making Oulton Park a truly immersive motorsport experience.
trackCharacter: The International layout at Oulton Park is a true test of driver skill and car setup. Its blend of fast straights, challenging corners, and significant elevation changes demands precision, commitment, and bravery. The circuit rewards a well-balanced car with good mechanical grip and strong braking performance. Unlike some of the faster, more flowing circuits, Oulton Park requires drivers to constantly adjust their driving style to suit the varying demands of each section. It's a circuit where overtaking is difficult, but rewarding when executed perfectly, and where mistakes are heavily punished.

famousCorners.name: Old Hall Corner
famousCorners.description: The first corner, a deceptively tight right-hander that immediately sorts out the brave from the tentative. It's crucial to get a good exit to carry speed onto the run down to Cascades.
famousCorners.challenge: Demands pinpoint accuracy and commitment. It's easy to run wide on the exit, compromising the following section.

famousCorners.name: Cascades
famousCorners.description: A fast, downhill left-hander that requires nerves of steel. It's a real test of a car's aerodynamic grip and balance.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining speed and control through this corner is essential for a quick lap time. Overdriving it can lead to a costly spin or off-track excursion.

famousCorners.name: Knickerbrook
famousCorners.description: A complex sequence of corners that demands precision and rhythm. It’s a challenging section that requires a well-balanced car.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining momentum and avoiding mistakes through this section is key. Any error here can ruin a lap.

famousCorners.name: Druids
famousCorners.description: A tight hairpin bend that is a prime overtaking spot. It requires heavy braking and precise placement of the car.
famousCorners.challenge: Braking late and maintaining control under pressure is crucial. It's easy to lock up the brakes or run wide, opening the door for an overtake.

famousCorners.name: Lodge
famousCorners.description: A deceptive left-hand corner that leads onto the long run to Deer Leap, offering a chance to gain time if taken perfectly.
famousCorners.challenge: This corner requires a very late apex and a lot of commitment, it's essential to carry as much speed as possible onto the straight.

historySnippets: Oulton Park was built on the site of a former World War II army camp.
The first race at Oulton Park was held in August 1953.
Stirling Moss won the Gold Cup at Oulton Park four times.
The International layout is the longest configuration at Oulton Park.
Oulton Park has hosted rounds of the British Touring Car Championship since 1960s.
Several Formula 1 teams have used Oulton Park for testing purposes in the past.
weatherNotes: Oulton Park is located in a region known for unpredictable weather. Rain is a frequent occurrence, and the track can quickly become treacherous, especially in the wooded sections. Fog can also be a problem, particularly in the mornings. The changing weather conditions can significantly impact car setup and tire choice, making it a challenging venue for teams and drivers alike.
drivingAdvice: Mastering the International layout at Oulton Park requires a smooth and precise driving style. It's essential to carry momentum through the corners and avoid any unnecessary wheelspin. Pay close attention to the track limits, as running wide can be heavily penalized. Be prepared to adapt to changing weather conditions, and don't be afraid to experiment with different lines to find the optimal racing line. Patience is key, as overtaking opportunities are limited, but rewarding when executed perfectly.
famousRaces: BTCC: The British Touring Car Championship races at Oulton Park are always action-packed, with close battles and dramatic incidents.
British GT: The British GT Championship races showcase high-performance sports cars battling for supremacy on the challenging circuit.
British Superbikes: The British Superbike Championship events draw huge crowds, with thrilling motorcycle racing action around every corner.
Gold Cup: Historic races are held here on the 'Historic' layout, celebrating the circuit's heritage.
localCulture: Cheshire is a county known for its picturesque countryside, historic market towns, and vibrant cultural scene. The local area surrounding Oulton Park offers a range of attractions, including historic houses, gardens, and museums. The paddock atmosphere is friendly and welcoming, with teams and drivers often mingling with fans. Local delicacies include Cheshire cheese, and traditional pub fare is readily available in the nearby villages.
